gen-gf-esteban-fs-supreme: Refined and bookish, Esteban lets its curves thin out at the tops of the rounds, while Supreme lays down a dense, crisp band beneath. Their gap in touch is the whole appeal.
gen-gf-esteban-manrope: Manrope reads bright and approachable, its curves wide open at the mouth. Esteban above it brings a gentle, bookish serif touch, and if the heading shrinks too small, that softness stops showing.
gen-gf-esteban-montserrat: Montserrat glides along like fine wire, with generous counters and every round and stem in a single weight. Esteban, the serif heading, adds a faintly modulated, steady line above it, so the page moves from bookish to geometric.
gen-gf-esteban-satoshi: A quiet shift in line weight, like brushed watercolor, marks Esteban's serif letters. Satoshi follows with a soaring x-height and a plain sans stroke that never changes thickness, so a long passage moves smoothly.
gen-gf-esteban-switzer: Approachable and Swiss, Switzer holds its c tips well apart and draws tubular, wire-like letters. And Esteban, refined and bookish, thins its joins gently above them, giving the serif and sans-serif a clear division of roles.
gen-gf-fanwood-text-archivo: Archivo brings a commanding x-height and curves that open outward instead of curling in. Archivo then carries a longer stretch of text with an editorial confidence, while Fanwood Text sits above it with classic ease.
gen-gf-fanwood-text-fs-asap: Fanwood Text has a classic, editorial look, its arches thinning slightly as they leave the stem, over Asap's open-arc forms. Size Asap up, since its body height nearly matches the capitals.
gen-gf-fanwood-text-fs-epilogue: Short-looking ascenders give Fanwood Text its distinctive profile, since the lowercase body stands so tall. But Epilogue, a contemporary sans with a wire-like monoline skeleton, keeps a longer passage feeling loose and approachable.
gen-gf-fanwood-text-fs-public-sans: Classic type, hefty body. Fanwood Text carries a subtle pen-like modulation in its bowls, so let Public Sans, the sans-serif with broad open counters, be the one you enlarge.
gen-gf-fanwood-text-fs-supreme: Fanwood Text has short-looking ascenders, because its lowercase body is so tall, and its weight shifts modestly across each curve. Supreme, a plain sans with a thick, crisp strip through the middle, makes the contrast the pair's strongest quality.
